A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EGENNET research and contain complete, readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–I. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original EGENNET experiments on synthetic graph separation and chemical property prediction, plus runtime and molecular norm analyses in Appendix I.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results in Section 6 and Appendix I.

M1.justification: The EGENNET aggregation, invariant readout, and activation choices in Section 5.1 remain unchanged. Appendix H retains the same extension incorporating node and edge features.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same graph pairs, 4-chain and 12-chain tasks, four challenging point-cloud pairs, and Drugs, Kraken, and BDE chemical prediction datasets.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding experiments in Tables 1–7, including SchNet variants, equivariant separation models, and molecular and conformer-ensemble baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B retains the same splits, model configurations, and training procedures, including the chemical tasks' 70/10/20 split and 1,500 epochs. Table 5's revised accuracy caption clarifies the existing metric without changing evaluation.

E4.justification: The power-graph comparisons, layer-depth experiments, challenging separation cases, and molecular norm-threshold analysis are retained without additional or revised analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose ten seeds for power-graph and chain experiments and three runs for chemical prediction. Best-validation-run reporting and Appendix I's means and standard deviations are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results and findings are unchanged. For example, both report EGENNET BDE MAE 0.3170 in Table 2 and 0.4455 ± 0.1305 in Table 6. Added trailing zeros in Table 5 and revised numerical notation in Table 8 preserve the same values.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, Theorems 3.1–5.1, Corollary 5.2, and mathematical developments and proofs in Appendices C–H are unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions make the same claims about connectivity enabling generic equivariant separation, global rigidity governing invariant separation, and EGENNET achieving generic maximal expressivity with competitive empirical performance.

C2.justification: The interpretations involving reduced over-squashing and near-generic molecular geometry remain unchanged. Section 7 retains the limitation concerning symmetric and non-generic inputs and the same future-work direction.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, software, and NVIDIA A40 hardware disclosures are unchanged. The abstract replaces the displayed repository URL with 'GitHub', but the underlying link points to the same repository.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive research positioning are unchanged, including Appendix A's comparison with Wang and Zhang and the distinctions from previous completeness results.

P1.justification: v5 revises the author and affiliation block, adds author emails, makes small grammatical corrections, clarifies the Table 5 cross-reference, and rewrites several captions. The section sequence and scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 5 replaces colored cells with bold best scores and standardized decimal precision. Tables 7–8 receive more compact layouts and revised captions and notation. Footnote styling and page spacing change; the figures and table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves presentation: Table 5 explicitly identifies accuracy and chance-level performance, highlights best scores, and standardizes precision; Tables 7–8 are more compact. These changes improve readability, while the scientific content, evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
